models.name: Qwen 3.5 4B
models.primary_use: Incumbent fast lane — OpenClaw routing, fast tool calls, edge
models.note: Feb 2026 release, swapped into agentic_light on 2026-05-10 (role pointer moved to the no-think alias qwen35_4b_nothink on 2026-08-12, #489 — same weights). Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + sparse MoE on a 4B base, 262k native ctx, 201 languages incl. ES/CA. No 4B-class challenger shipped through September 2026 — both of this window's new text entrants landed in Tier B/C.

models.name: Qwen3 4B (2507)
models.note: Solid small agentic model from late 2025. Dominated by Qwen 3.5 4B on context, multilingual reach, and quality.

models.name: Gemma 3 4B
models.primary_use: Fast multilingual triage, transcript shaping, Catalan
models.note: Best Catalan support of the small models. Weaker function calling than Qwen3.5. Useful as a CPU-side translation specialist on the 7800X3D.

models.name: Phi-4 Mini
models.note: Speed king in the small tier, but multilingual gap rules it out for ES/CA.

models.name: Llama 3.2 3B
models.note: Dominated. 2026 community testing reports unreliable triage / hallucinated replies.

models.name: Granite 4.1 8B
models.note: Late-Apr 2026 release; strong enterprise tool-calling in the 8B class (est. composite — headline numbers are coding-weighted, which this stack ignores). Dominated by Qwen 3.5 4B on speed and Qwen3.5 9B on quality at similar VRAM.

models.name: Ministral 3 14B
models.note: Dec 2025 release. Good European multilingual incl. ES, 256k ctx — but dominated by GPT-OSS 20B and the tier-B MoEs on both chart axes.

models.name: Qwen3.5 9B
models.note: Confirmed 250k+ context on this exact GPU. Loses to Gemma 4 26B MoE and Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B on speed AND quality.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B Unified
models.note: Released 2026-06-03. Encoder-free multimodal: text, image, and native AUDIO input straight into the backbone; 140 languages; benchmark coverage 'nearing the 26B' (est. composite 76, tps est. from Gemma 3 12B). Dominated on both chart axes by Gemma 4 26B MoE — its niche is the ~7 GB footprint and native-audio input, neither of which the current roles need.

models.name: Gemma 3 12B
models.note: Dominated by Gemma 4 26B MoE on every axis, and by Gemma 4 12B Unified within its own size class.

models.name: Mistral Small 3.2
models.note: Strong European multilingual but dominated on speed by MoE alternatives.

models.name: GPT-OSS 20B
models.note: Excellent BFCL/τ-bench, native MXFP4 fits 16 GB. MMMLU Spanish 79.7 (medium reasoning) confirmed 2026-07-24 — decent, not leading. Catalan still unverified.

models.name: Gemma 4 26B MoE
models.primary_use: Incumbent workhorse — transcripts, documents, deep agentic, EN↔ES↔CA
models.note: Still the standout 16 GB-class model as of September 2026. Tie with Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B persists through six consecutive runs. Two new entrants this window — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (SSD-paged n-gram table caps real speed at dense-27B levels) and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (doesn't fit 16 GB cleanly, unverified speed, unverified Catalan) — both dominated. GLM-5.3, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash stay confirmed NO-GOs.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B
models.primary_use: Tied with Gemma 4 26B MoE — agentic, long-doc, 201-language multilingual
models.note: Released 2026-04-16; still the newest locally-runnable Apache-2.0 MoE at this VRAM class as of September 2026. Composite within ~1% of Gemma 4 26B → tie stands.

models.name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B-A3B)
models.note: New — shipped 2026-08-11, missed by the 2026-08-20 run (sourcing-gap catch, same pattern as Nemotron 3 Nano 4B's #486). Doesn't fit 16 GB VRAM at any published quant (Q4_0 ~18.9 GB + 1.16 GB MTP, Q4_K_M ~25.5 GB); an MoE-CPU-offload split (same -ot pattern this repo uses for glm) is untested on any 16 GB-class card — the one public benchmark (123 t/s) used an RTX 5090 with no offload needed. Documented languages (EN/ES/FR/DE/IT/JA) omit Catalan, the same axis where its smaller Nemotron 3 Nano 4B sibling was locally disproven (#486). tps/quality are estimates pending a local test — see report §4/§9.

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
models.arch: MoE (sparse, 512 experts, 10 routed + 1 shared) + n-gram embedding + MTP
models.note: New 2026-08-26 — Alibaba's preview of the Qwen4 architecture. The 51B-parameter n-gram embedding table pages from SSD on every request, capping real-world decode speed at dense-27B-class levels (17-23 t/s measured in community testing) despite the 6B-active MoE design — the headline efficiency never reaches the token stream. Dominated on speed by both Tier B MoE leaders at a fraction of the footprint, and by Qwen3 32B dense at less VRAM. Quality is an estimate; license is Qwen Community 1.0, not Apache 2.0.

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B (dense)
models.note: Shipped 2026-08-14. Native text/image/video input, strong reported instruction-following, but headline gains are coding/agentic-coding benchmarks at 0% weight here. Dense architecture loses the decode-speed race to both MoE leaders by ~3-4x at a comparable VRAM footprint. Quality is an estimate. Dominated on speed; not recommended.

models.name: Qwen 3.6 27B (dense)
models.note: Dominated by the 35B-A3B MoE sibling on speed AND quality at the same VRAM footprint — MoE wins on this hardware. Same fate as its Qwen3.8-27B successor.

models.name: Gemma 3 27B (dense)
models.note: Dominated by Gemma 4 26B MoE: same family, higher quality, ~6× faster decode thanks to MoE.

models.name: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
models.note: Predecessor to Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B. Dominated by the 3.6 update on speed and benchmark scores at lower VRAM.

models.name: Qwen3 32B (dense)
models.primary_use: Quality runs, hard agentic, batch overnight
models.note: BFCL v3 leader among open weights (75.7%). ~3.5 GB CPU spill, ~10–12 t/s. Held off the Tier B frontier by Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B which matches its quality at ~9× the speed. Still beats every Tier C entrant evaluated to date on verified speed.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.note: No update this window. Real published GGUF sizes (162 GB lossless 8-bit, 103 GB community 3-bit) fit this box's ~144 GB combined budget at 3-bit. Still not recommended: no first-party non-coding composite quality evidence, and the vendor's 'DSpark' 2x decode claim is unverified locally.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5
models.note: Dense 128B is too large for this box even with 128 GB RAM offload — single-digit t/s. Modified MIT license has revenue gates. Dropped on hardware grounds, not quality.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.note: Heavy CPU offload (24 GB+ in RAM). Dominated by Qwen3 32B: faster AND higher quality at lower VRAM.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro-0813
models.note: No update this window. 49B active params alone implies a footprint far past this box's ~144 GB budget even at aggressive quantization. NO-GO on hardware grounds. Not chart-plotted at a realistic operating point; listed for completeness.

models.name: Qwen3.8 2.4T-A95B (open flagship)
models.note: No update this window. 95B active params alone puts it an order of magnitude past this box's budget. NO-GO on hardware grounds. Not chart-plotted at a realistic operating point; listed for completeness.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.note: No update this window. Still an order of magnitude past this box's ~144 GB combined VRAM+RAM. Not chart-plotted at a realistic operating point; listed for completeness only.

models.name: GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3
models.note: Standing NO-GO carried from prior runs (docs/glm-5.2-evaluation.md, #141): >1 TB VRAM in BF16, smallest useful quant ~245 GB combined vs this box's ~144 GB. GLM-5.5 flagship still rumored (JPMorgan research note, 2026-06-25) but has no model card, benchmark, or endpoint yet — watch next cycle.

asr_models.name: Parakeet TDT v3 (Mac ANE)
asr_models.tagline: Primary since 2026-07-22 — placement/latency swap, not accuracy
asr_models.note: Unchanged incumbent since #350. Fastest STT in the fleet — 65.8× RTFx, sub-second even on 108 s clips. Published MLS/FLEURS Spanish WER modestly beats Whisper Large v3 — but this project's own jargon-heavy dictation-domain testing (docs/parakeet-asr-evaluation.md) shows the reverse: 2-4x worse WER, drops the 'Claude Code' wake phrase entirely, mangles 'YOLO'->'yellow'. The identified fix (FluidAudio CustomVocabularyContext) was built and disproven 2026-07-24 (#401). No fix currently exists via FluidAudio; Granite Speech 4.1 2B is a promising untested alternative architecture.

asr_models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo (failover)
asr_models.note: Unchanged. Still the accuracy leader on this domain thanks to the #91 --carry-initial-prompt boosting glossary — a lever Parakeet structurally lacks (no decode-time TDT biasing hook exists in FluidAudio).

asr_models.name: IBM Granite Speech 4.1 2B
asr_models.languages: EN, ES, FR, DE, PT, JA
asr_models.tagline: New lead — decode-time keyword biasing, unlike Parakeet's post-hoc rescorer
asr_models.note: New this window — supersedes the 8B-class Granite Speech 3.3 this report previously carried (5.85% WER); now leads the public HF Open ASR Leaderboard at 5.33% WER at a quarter of the parameter count. Keyword-list biasing runs as prompt-conditioned decode-time steering through its LLM decoder — structurally distinct from FluidAudio's post-hoc CTC rescoring, which #401 proved cannot insert a phrase the acoustic model dropped entirely. Untested against this project's #138/#343 jargon corpus; recommended next local smoke test before any verdict change (report §7.1/§7.2.1/§9).

asr_models.name: Parakeet + FluidAudio CustomVocabularyContext
asr_models.note: FluidAudio's only vocabulary mechanism is a post-hoc CTC rescorer that can swap an emitted word for a similar one — it cannot insert a phrase the TDT decoder dropped entirely. v0.15.5/0.15.6 (this window) added per-term CTC thresholds and opt-in knobs — a refinement of the same mechanism, not a decode-time hook. Re-open trigger not met; carried watch per docs/frontier/local-findings.md.

asr_models.name: faster-whisper Turbo (CTranslate2)
asr_models.tagline: Disproven locally (#274) — no longer the primary's concern
asr_models.note: Measured 1.0x speedup (not the claimed ~2x), WER parity-to-worse, drops the 'Claude Code' wake phrase 0/2 across an 18-attempt sweep. Carried watch per docs/frontier/local-findings.md (#277). Relevant only to the whisper failover leg's own engine, not the live primary.

asr_models.name: faster-whisper Large v3
asr_models.tagline: Use for ES → EN single-pass translation
asr_models.note: Higher accuracy than Turbo and supports task=translate. Fallback for workload G when the LLM slot is busy.

asr_models.name: Qwen3-ASR (1.7B / MLX build)
asr_models.tagline: Watch — generic WER improved, no domain-specific comparison exists
asr_models.note: No change this window. FluidAudio still has no Qwen3-ASR backend (#676, removed) and no jargon-domain comparison exists — the exact generic-vs-domain gap that made Parakeet's own leaderboard numbers misleading (see 7.2.1). Smoke-test locally before trusting any published number for this workload.

asr_models.name: NVIDIA Canary-Qwen 2.5B
asr_models.note: #1 on HF Open ASR Leaderboard at 5.63% WER (English-only track), but English-strong with very limited Spanish support.

asr_translation_paths.label: Architecture (i) — Single-model
asr_translation_paths.headline: faster-whisper Large v3 with task=translate
asr_translation_paths.pros: Simplest pipeline, ~2 GB VRAM, ~30× realtime, single pass
asr_translation_paths.cons: Literal English output. No style polish, no summarization, occasional idiom loss.
asr_translation_paths.verdict: Fallback when LLM slot is occupied

asr_translation_paths.label: Architecture (ii) — Two-stage
asr_translation_paths.headline: faster-whisper Turbo (ES) → Gemma 4 26B MoE (translate + polish + disfluency)
asr_translation_paths.pros: Higher quality, context-aware translation, polishing + filler removal in same LLM call. Catalan extension comes free.
asr_translation_paths.cons: ~15 GB VRAM total — fast-lane model drops out for batches.

disfluency_verdict.decision: Fold into the LLM polishing pass
disfluency_verdict.reasoning: Specialized disfluency-removal models (DisfluencyFixer, DISCO) are research-grade and primarily EN/HI/DE/FR — Spanish coverage is sparse. Tier-B LLMs (Gemma 4 26B MoE, Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B) handle disfluency removal extremely well as part of an instruction-following pass. Adding a separate component means another model loaded, another VRAM slot, another point of failure, and worse multilingual coverage than the LLM you already run.
disfluency_verdict.prompt:
Clean up this transcript:
- Remove filler words (um, uh, eh, este, like, you know)
- Remove false starts and self-corrections, keep the corrected version
- Tighten conciseness without losing meaning or voice
- Preserve technical terms and proper nouns exactly
- Keep the output in [Spanish/English] — do not translate

{transcript}

concurrency_recipes.label: Recipe 1 — Two lanes
concurrency_recipes.note: Both at full speed. Total ~17 GB — minor shared-memory spill, handled gracefully on Blackwell. Tower GPU is exclusively agentic since the 2026-07-22 audio placement move (#343).

concurrency_recipes.label: Recipe 2 — Qwen 3.6 stack (Apache 2.0 only)
concurrency_recipes.note: All-Apache stack — useful when license clarity matters (Macaya Bank work). Speed parity with Recipe 1.

concurrency_recipes.label: Recipe 3 — Quality batch
concurrency_recipes.summary: Qwen 3.5 4B (GPU) + Qwen3 32B dense (GPU + ~3.5 GB CPU spill).
concurrency_recipes.note: Fast lane unaffected. 32B at ~10 t/s — overnight transcript reprocessing.

concurrency_recipes.label: Recipe 4 — Three concurrent
concurrency_recipes.note: The 7800X3D's 96 MB L3 makes Gemma 3 4B on CPU run ~10 t/s — useful as a Catalan-strong specialist.

top_picks.why: Best small agentic model on this hardware as of September 2026 — and still the incumbent. Hybrid DeltaNet + sparse MoE, 262k native ctx, 201 languages, Apache 2.0. No 4B-class challenger has shipped.

99 t/s, full 256k context, Google-grade multilingual including Catalan. Tie with Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B persists through six consecutive runs — keep Gemma as default on Catalan track record; switch to Qwen 3.6 if you need pure Apache 2.0. Both MoE leaders beat this window's new entrants (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning) on verified/fitting speed.
BFCL leader at 75.7%. ~10 t/s with mild CPU spill — reserve for batch quality runs where correctness > latency. Still beats every other Tier C entrant evaluated to date on verified speed.

agentic_light.reason: Incumbent (model swapped in 2026-05-10; role pointer moved to this no-think alias 2026-08-12 via #489, same underlying weights) is still the Tier A Pareto pick: ~110 t/s, ~3 GB, 262k native ctx, 201 languages, Apache 2.0. Neither of this window's new text entrants (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning) is 4B-class — no challenger this tier.

agentic_heavy.reason: Incumbent and Tier B top pick; tie (≤3%) with Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B persists through six consecutive runs. Two genuine new entrants this window — Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (180B/6B active, shipped 2026-08-26) and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B/3B active, shipped 2026-08-11, a sourcing-gap catch from #486's pattern) — are both dominated: Flash-Next's 51B-param n-gram table pages from SSD and caps real speed at dense-27B levels despite the MoE label; Lightning doesn't fit 16 GB VRAM at any published quant, has no tok/s measurement on comparable hardware, ships under a non-Apache license (OpenMDW-1.1), and its documented languages (EN/ES/FR/DE/IT/JA) omit Catalan — the same gap that sank its disproven Nemotron 3 Nano 4B sibling (#486). Not recommended without a local test.

audio_transcribe.reason: No verified fix this window, but the most promising lead in months surfaced: Granite Speech 4.1 2B (IBM, Apache 2.0) now leads the public HF Open ASR Leaderboard at 5.33% WER and implements keyword-list biasing as prompt-conditioned decode-time steering through its LLM decoder — structurally distinct from the post-hoc CTC rescoring that FluidAudio's CustomVocabularyContext uses and that #401 proved incapable of inserting a dropped phrase. Untested against this project's #138/#343 jargon corpus, so verdict stays watch — this project has been burned twice recommending ASR benchmark claims that didn't survive local domain testing (#274, #401). Recommended next step: a local smoke test, not a role change.

audio_translate.reason: Unchanged: the two-stage path (Turbo → Gemma 4 26B MoE) stays the default for ES→EN; whisper-medium remains a lazy-loaded fallback for when the LLM slot is busy. Granite Speech 4.1 2B's native bidirectional ES↔EN speech translation is a candidate to eventually replace the fallback leg's engine (smaller and higher-ranked than whisper-medium) but is untested here — no change to the default this run.
